This role will lead and coordinate communications for a portfolio of complex change programmes and projects, helping staff and stakeholders understand and engage with institutional change. UCSO provides expertise in change and communications, benefits realisation, portfolio planning, common standards, strategic reporting and business-case appraisal. It supports the Change and Programme Management Board in directing and overseeing the University's portfolio of major change programmes, for which communications is a key enabling function. Working within the strategic communications direction and the established operational priorities, the post-holder will develop, implement and evaluate communications approaches for UCSO-supported change activity. The role will provide specialist advice on stakeholder engagement, messaging, timing, channels, listening mechanisms and communications risks, including where issues are sensitive or operationally significant. The post-holder will also serve as the UCSO communications practice lead for change activity, developing standards, tools and templates; coordinating communications across programmes; coaching contributors; and using audience insight and feedback to improve communications impact. The role will work closely with programme teams, Change Partners, communications colleagues and the University's Internal Communications Team within the Office of External Affairs and Communications. Key responsibilities Develop, implement and evaluate internal communications strategies and stakeholder engagement plans for UCSO-supported change activity, translating programme objectives into clear messages, channels, listening arrangements and impact measures. Provide specialist communications advice to programme boards, senior responsible officers, committees, managers and programme teams on sensitive messaging, timing, stakeholder confidence, reputational considerations and adoption risks. Define and embed communications standards, tools, templates and quality criteria, and support consistent practice across programmes through coaching, feedback and practical guidance. Coordinate communications across UCSO-supported programmes, Reimagining Professional Service activity and other major change initiatives, aligning messages and schedules and resolving duplication or conflicting communications needs. Produce, commission, edit and assure high-quality communications products, and use audience insight, channel information and stakeholder feedback to identify risks and improve communications effectiveness. About you You will: Have significant experience of leading or coordinating communications for complex organisational change, transformation, policy implementation or institutional programmes involving multiple stakeholder groups. Bring advanced knowledge of internal and change communications, with experience of advising senior stakeholders on sensitive communications, engagement, messaging, timing and reputational considerations. Have excellent written, verbal and editorial judgement and experience of producing or assuring high-impact content for specialist and non-specialist audiences. Be able to develop practical communications strategies, standards and evaluation approaches, interpret audience insight and feedback, and influence effectively through matrix working arrangements. Be educated to degree level, or have equivalent practical experience, in communications, engagement, public relations, journalism, marketing, organisational change or a related field. A recognised professional communications qualification is desirable. The Benefits In return, you will receive an extensive reward and benefits package including: 41 days annual leave, including bank holidays. Potential for flexible and hybrid working, subject to the operational needs of the role. A generous pension scheme, discount portal, cycle to work scheme, access to the University accommodation service, relocation expenses scheme, employee assistance programme and family-friendly policies. The funds for this post are available for 3 years in the first instance. Applications are welcome from internal candidates who would like to apply for the role on the basis of a secondment from their current role in the University. We welcome applications from individuals who wish to be considered for part-time working or other flexible working arrangements. Candidates will be shortlisted and invited to interview based upon these criteria. Interviews will be held in late November 2026. Additional information regarding the role can be found within the further information file. If you wish to discuss this role in more detail, or have questions about the application process, enquiries are welcome. Please contact the team via change@admin.cam.ac.uk. Please quote reference YV51402 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. right there|glasgow.description: About The Role Are you an ambitious communications leader who wants your work to change lives? If the answer is yes, this could be the opportunity you have been waiting for. Bring your creativity, judgement and leadership to Right There and help make our impact impossible to ignore. For over 200 years, Right There has helped prevent people becoming homeless and keep families together across Scotland. Last year alone, over 4,000 people received the support they needed to stay in their homes and close to the people they love. We have a proud history, an urgent mission and the ambition to reach even further. Now we need an exceptional communications leader to illuminate our work, strengthen trust in Right There and inspire the support that will make even greater impact possible. This is a high-profile leadership opportunity at the heart of Right There. As a member of our Senior Management Team, you will influence organisational strategy, shape how Scotland understands our work and build the audiences, profile and support we need to achieve lasting change. You will have the freedom and influence to strengthen our brand, bring our impact vividly to life and ensure that the voices and experiences of the people we support are heard with care and authenticity. This is an ambitious role with the scope to build understanding, challenge assumptions and use outstanding communications to help create lasting change. Your role Your first opportunity will be to bring our marketing, communications, PR, public affairs and digital activity together behind Our compelling vision. You will give Right There a clearer, stronger and more distinctive voice, while ensuring that everything we communicate remains rooted in the real experiences of the people we support. Setting the direction. You will set the strategic direction for communications, public affairs and supporter engagement, building Right There’s profile, influence and connection with the people and communities we want to reach. Joining up our activity. You will turn organisational priorities into clear, audience-led plans and deliver an integrated marketing and communications strategy with meaningful measures of awareness, engagement, influence and support. Building our voice and influence. You will lead policy, press and public affairs activity so Right There is recognised as a credible voice and contributes meaningfully to debates affecting the people we support. Connecting people to our work. You will shape internal communications, develop our website and content strategy, and make it easy for colleagues, supporters and communities to understand our priorities, programmes and impact. Leading with care and confidence. You will develop a creative, high-performing team and set clear standards so communications are accessible and ethical. What you bring You will already be an accomplished leader in marketing, communications or PR, ideally within a charity or social-purpose organisation, and you will be ready to bring that experience to a mission with real urgency. You will combine strategic ambition with humanity: making thoughtful decisions, building respectful relationships and creating communications that honour the dignity, strengths and experiences of the people we support. You have led integrated, multi-channel activity across digital, social media, PR, content and campaigns. You can translate strategy into high-quality work that reaches audiences and delivers measurable results. You bring strong editorial judgement and experience of shaping brands, messages and media relationships. You use insight and analytics to improve performance and ensure communications are accessible, ethical and appropriate for sensitive subject matter. You are a motivating and inclusive leader with compassion, curiosity and a genuine belief in the power of people’s stories. Your application As part of your application, please submit a cover letter. It will form a significant part of our shortlisting decision, so tell us why this opportunity matters to you and use relevant examples to bring your skills, judgement, leadership approach and impact to life. We welcome creativity, but please write in your own words so your application genuinely reflects your experience, voice and perspective. Help us get to know you before we meet you. Our offer This is a full-time role working 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday. You will be based at 15 Dava Street in Glasgow, with a hybrid approach that combines around three office days each week with flexibility to work remotely. Our offer includes six weeks’ annual leave pro rata, rising to eight weeks after your first year, membership of the People’s Pension, a cycle-to-work scheme and the option to purchase or sell annual leave. If you are ready to use the power of communications to build understanding, challenge assumptions and help create lasting change across Scotland, we want to hear from you. About Us We are a charity that recently celebrated 200 years of standing alongside people in Scotland. Last year we supported over 4,000 people to stay in their homes and stay connected to the people they love.
